subject.parentsPinned: 15/15 parent pins and both chapter-14 override before-texts match byte-exact

verdictSummary: Not an adequate complete report owner. The candidate is a sound partial shape contract: pins, renderer gating, envelope closure, graph run pinning, no-latest history and the three limit layers hold. It does not close AUDIT-G10 as claimed. fit HTML is knowingly undeliverable, yet admission accepts a fit document. Envelope4 in-document joins are not admitted. A real subject3/endpoint identity join is declared nonexistent. Several required inventory features vanish as 'not projected' with no typed disclosure. The report codec admits records their own owner codec refuses. Byte budgets are derived from representative, not worst-case, owner payloads. Design completion is not established. Product qualification (RP-OBL-2) was correctly kept separate and is not assessed.

requiredFindings.title: RP-OBL-1: fit HTML is knowingly undeliverable but is presented as covered, and admission accepts a fit document missing required parity
evidence: inventory4 fit row parityFields = run-id, candidates, evidence-levels, termination-class, capability-availability; formats include html; no queryDispatch.

envelope4 has no candidate carrier for kind=run, so fit parity is not total for any renderer (JSON included). No prior implementation record registers this gap (search of /tmp/opensip-implementation and docs/implementation outside this candidate found none).

The schema fit branch freezes envelope.kind to run|failure and supportedReportViews to overview, evidence, catalog, graph, symbol-detail. It has no findings view and no candidate view, so a successor carrier cannot be rendered under :1 (probe P11: SCHEMA refusal).

The subject's own positive case positive-fit-budget-omission is admitted: kind=run, envelope keys contain no candidates or evidenceLevels. check.py asserts the gap exists (check.py:332-334) and still passes. Reproduced in the review copy (probe P1: accept).
Prototype inventory R24 fit row requires 'Selected fit results in the common findings/evidence projection' and 'Preserve applicable fit HTML and parity fields'.
requiredFindings.requiredCorrection: Scoped correction, not a silent deferral. (a) State in the contract, successor.json scope and schema description that fit HTML is BLOCKED and AUDIT-G10 is not closed for fit. (b) Make admission refuse any fit document with envelope.kind=run until an envelope/inventory successor selects the candidate carrier. Remove or convert the fit positive case into a refusal case with a stable code. (c) Do not freeze a fit view/kind set that excludes candidate and findings presentation; defer the fit branch to the successor. (d) Register the envelope4/inventory4 fit-carrier defect with its owner as a blocking gap that affects JSON/human/agent as well as HTML.

requiredFindings.title: Functions table / symbol detail: the claimed absence of a subject3<->GraphEndpoint join is false; the needed finite projection is missing
evidence: identity-schemas.v3 evaluation-subject = {schemaVersion:3, universe, kind in file|symbol|package, nativeSubjectId Text<=4096, packageManifestPath iff package}. graph-query:3 GraphEndpoint = {universe, kind StoredKind file|symbol|package, nativeSubjectId <=4096, packageManifestPath iff package}. The member sets and bounds are identical.

The typed identifier is ID(D,X) = prefix + ':' + hex(H(D,X)), with H over the exact canonical bytes. The evaluator reference models mint subject3 exactly as M.identifier('evaluation-subject', {schemaVersion:3, universe, kind, nativeSubjectId}).

So the host can mint the subject3 of every embedded endpoint under an existing identity owner and join FindingSurface.subjectId exactly. SubjectId's 'must not unpack' law forbids only the reverse direction.

The contract instead declares 'No subject3<->endpoint join exists'. R11 then keeps only 'findings shown separately', and R07 degree counts are unjoined to findings, losing the required exact Run/universe/symbol binding and cross-view navigation.
requiredFindings.requiredCorrection: Add a finite host projection, e.g. GraphSubjectIndexV1 in the graph panel: a sorted unique list of {endpoint, subjectId}, one row per distinct embedded endpoint, bounded by the slot bounds. subjectId is host-minted as ID('evaluation-subject', {schemaVersion:3, ...endpoint}). Admission recomputes every row, refuses duplicates or mismatches, and never derives an endpoint from a subjectId. Symbol-detail and functions views join findings by exact subjectId equality only; body-hash, path or name matching stays forbidden. Degree counts stay labelled 'embedded subset'.

requiredFindings.title: Required inventory features disappear under 'no owner' with no typed document disclosure and no registered obligation
evidence: R07 requires metrics and test reachability bound to exact identity and 'show unknown values'. The contract says they have no owner and are not shown. The review's search of the pinned owner schemas found no metrics or test-reachability owner, so the absence is real, but the inventory still requires a visible unknown state.

R05 requires 'selected policy/capability descriptions'. R06 requires 'recipe names, descriptions, selectors and applicable parameters' and says 'unavailable catalog data has an explicit state'. The contract shows neither and adds no state.

R03 requires the Invocation/step/attempt ledger with missing child evidence. The contract says it is not projected because kind=invocation has no HTML, yet audit runs two analysis steps plus a comparison step and analyze runs import+analysis.
R23  declared configuration: 'no redaction owner; not projected', again with no disclosure.
None of these appear in openObligations (RP-OBL-1..4). check.py:347 accepts any nonempty presentationalOnly string as a complete mapping, so featureMap coverage is tautological for these rows.
requiredFindings.requiredCorrection: Each missing feature needs a finite typed, per-view disclosure in the document, for example a schema-constant list per command of {featureId: R03-step-ledger|R05-descriptions|R06-recipe-descriptions|R06-recipe-parameters|R07-metrics|R07-test-reachability|R23-declared-configuration, state: unavailable, reason: no-admitted-owner}. The browser renders it as an explicit unknown/unavailable state. Also register one owner obligation per feature and exclude those rows from any 'complete R01-R24 mapping' claim. check.py must refuse a featureMap row whose required-data items are satisfied only by prose.

requiredFindings.title: Panels are described as exact admitted owner records while source identity is unbound; admission accepts substitution
evidence: Probe P10: capabilities declarations replaced by [] with a recomputed registrySha256 -> accept. registrySha256 is self-referential and binds to no release/closure identity of the Run.
Probe P4: comparison unavailable and history baselineId set to an arbitrary baseline2 -> accept. J-HISTORY-BASELINE runs only when comparison is present.
Probe P7: the history row's findings replaced by the current Run's findings -> accept. FindingSurface carries no runId, and no host obligation for history-finding provenance is declared.

The §6 host obligations list only the coverage stream, the baseline descriptor.runId and the effective policy. Registry provenance, history findings provenance and graph response provenance are not declared.

requiredFindings.title: The larger report codec overrides owner exact-codec laws; the report codec is not specified as a byte codec
evidence: maxJsonDepth 38 is applied uniformly, but embedding gains differ: envelope 1, coverage entry 5, policy rule 5, graph request/response 6, capability registry 6.

Probe P6: a PolicyDocumentV2 rule with notChain 28 is refused by its owner codec (DEPTH_LIMIT at 32) but admitted inside the report (accept). The window is notChain 28 for rules; an envelope-embedded structure gets up to 5 levels of slack.

check.py typed_report validates Python values only. Report admission never parses bytes (duplicate key, -0, float, UTF-8 strictness, parse-time byte limit), yet the chapter-14 override asserts 'the report-profile exact codec ... is applied before shape validation'.
RP-OBL-3 leaves that codec's semanticValidatorOwner unnamed.
requiredFindings.requiredCorrection: Specify the report-profile codec as a byte codec: the parse rules of canonical.py at documentMaxCanonicalBytes. Every embedded owner record must also satisfy its owner's exact-codec depth measured from its native offset (report depth <= offset + ownerMaxDepth - nativeOffset), so the larger profile never admits an owner-refused record or changes its identity bytes. Add lexical byte-level refusal cases and the notChain-28 refusal case. Name the validator owner before the chapter-14 line-556 override is applied.

requiredFindings.title: Budget constants are derived from representative samples; worst-case owner-valid payloads refute the stated derivations and the degradation laws
evidence: Worst-case owner-valid FindingSurface = 49,889 canonical bytes (qualifiedName/messageCode 4096 4-byte scalars, 16x255 path segments; validated) vs 759 used. 100,000 findings = 4,988,900,000 bytes vs envelopeMaxCanonicalBytes 83,886,080; only 1,681 worst-case findings fit.
Worst-case GraphNeighborRow = 66,236 bytes (validated) vs 635 used. One owner-valid 1000-row page = 66,236,000 bytes; only 63 rows fit explorationMaxCanonicalBytes.
A single worst-case 64-hop GraphPathRow = 6,414,670 bytes (validated), which alone exceeds the whole exploration ceiling.
Byte pressure cannot prefix-truncate evidence: item-limit requires embedded == 3956 (probe P9: J-EVIDENCE-COUNTS). Graph pages are embedded whole. So byte overflow always forces whole-panel omission.
The contract derives 'maxGraphSlots 6' and '100000 envelope4 findings' as if they were capacities.

requiredFindings.requiredCorrection: Restate every constant as a cap with its worst-case consequence, not a capacity. State explicitly that owner-valid envelope4 results above envelopeMaxCanonicalBytes are HTML required-delivery failures, and how that relates to JSON output limits. Add a byte-driven host projection cause (e.g. omissionCause 'byte-limit' with total/omitted counts) or a deterministic page-size selection law so byte pressure degrades lists before whole panels. Add worst-case construction cases to check.py alongside the representative ones.

requiredFindings.title: Standing overstates design completion
evidence: The contract says it 'closes AUDIT-G10' and lists the schema as a 'Complete closed owner schema'. Yet fit is blocked (RPR-1), the report codec owner is unnamed (RP-OBL-3), several required features are unowned (RPR-4), and the endpoint join is missing (RPR-3).

The AUDIT-G10 M1 decision forbids generating report.ts/output.rs report carriers as complete while the gap is open. The proposed chapter-14 overrides would name report-projection:1 as the generation source without recording the partial standing.
Measured product qualification is correctly separated (RP-OBL-2, acceptanceDoesNotQualifyProduct true). This finding concerns design completion only.
requiredFindings.requiredCorrection: Set standing to 'partial owner'. Keep AUDIT-G10 open with an explicit residual list (RPR-1..RPR-7 outcomes). Make the chapter-14 overrides conditional on that residual list, or annotate them so generation of report.ts cannot be recorded complete.

advisories.text: Browser failure states are underspecified. A document-level shape/compatibility failure is a report-data.ts display error, but nothing states what the static file shows when script execution, bundled assets or generated validation fail. The html parityRule is 'static single-file rendering of the envelope ... identical counts and identities', and R01 says asset absence must not masquerade as a valid report. Consider a required static (non-script) failure/parity notice.

R14: history is limited to the audit baseline source Run (maxHistoryRuns 1). The deferral of explicit multi-run selection to a command-owner successor is legitimate, since no command flag exists, but it is not registered as an obligation.

Probe P5: an audit report whose run lacks comparisonResultId with comparison omitted/not-selected and history present is admitted. audit always selects a comparison, and comparison-id is audit parity; consider forbidding not-selected for audit.

The prototype report inventory and chapter 14 both describe themselves as author proposals pending Claude review. This review treats R01-R24 as the currently selected design scope, because chapter 14 (lines 15-17) and M4 (implementation plan line 888) bind to them, not as independently accepted rows. The required findings stand either way: a report owner cannot claim completion over scope it silently drops.
The architecture checkout has uncommitted modifications to unrelated files. All 15 pinned parents are byte-exact, so this does not affect the review.
